_comment: Editorial content in config, not in Python (global rule 9): the vocabulary of concepts this repo has retired. A live document using a retired concept's phrases is describing something that no longer exists, which no citation guard can see — a pointer is a path, and a description is prose. tests/test_repo_hygiene.py::test_ldsm41_no_live_document_uses_retired_vocabulary reads this file. Phrases are matched case-insensitively as substrings; a match is a finding ONLY when the markdown block and sentence containing it hold none of the retirement_markers below, because naming a retired thing as history is exactly what the citation conventions in CLAUDE.md exist to keep writable. Keep phrases specific enough that an ordinary sentence cannot contain one. Add a concept when a batch retires one; each carries the date it was retired, so a future reader can tell a live prohibition from archaeology, the reason, which the failure message prints, and write_instead, which says how to say it as history.

concepts.reason: The three-agent workflow (Code, Docs and GitHub agents on per-role branches, bootstrapped into one worktree each) was retired by the MAW batch, with its document, its role prompts and its bootstrap script. Work happens on main or on a feature branch merged into it. A live document describing the split as current sends a reader to a workflow that has no branches, no prompts and no script.
concepts.write_instead: Name it as history, in the past tense, the way CLAUDE.md's 'Working agreements' section does: say the workflow was retired on 2026-11-09 and what replaced it.
concepts.allowed_in_comment: No per-document exemption, and none is available: the per-sentence retirement markers do that work, and a whole-document exemption would have hidden the docs/GEMINI.md sentence this guard exists to catch. tests/test_repo_hygiene.py asserts that no concept carries allowed_in, so adding one turns the suite red on purpose — the field is read by the scan only so that a future author who argues for an exemption has a mechanism to argue about, and must change that assertion to use it.

_retirement_markers_comment: A sentence holding any of these is read as history rather than as a description of current practice, so the retired phrases in it are allowed. retirement_markers are unconditional: they name the retirement itself ('retired', 'deleted', 'never existed', 'there are no'). reporting_markers are past-tense verbs of reporting, which make a sentence an account of what a document said rather than a description of how work is done — but they count only when NOT immediately preceded by one of reporting_marker_blockers, because a cold pass measured bare 'described' exempting the present-tense passive 'The Docs agent is described in AGENTS.md and owns every document.' The window is ONE MARKDOWN BLOCK, then one sentence inside it, over text with inline code spans stripped and newlines within the block flattened, so hard-wrapped prose is read whole, a phrase quoted inside backticks is not a description at all, and a marker in one table row does not exempt the next row. Two earlier windows were measured failing: the paragraph (mutation MH put the exact sentence this guard exists for back into docs/GEMINI.md and the guard stayed green, because the neighbouring bullet said 'retired'), and the flattened-document sentence (a cold pass then found the same defect passing as a table row, a bullet and a heading, none of which end in punctuation). tests/test_repo_hygiene.py asserts all three forms, asserts the blocked present-tense passives are findings, and asserts no marker occurs in ordinary current-tense prose.
